content: Sub-question 4 answered: does the chronicle's structured metadata beat pure semantic retrieval? Yes, as a TARGETED lever, not a blanket win. Built a metadata-aware index on the Jetson (8982 chunks into sovereign_chronicle_meta, lifting domain/layer/intensity/timestamp into queryable Chroma metadata) and compared pure-semantic vs a hybrid rerank (0.72*cosine + 0.18*query-tag-overlap + 0.05*intensity + 0.05*recency over a 40-chunk pool). Stable result across 5 runs: on the Mythos lineage query (sibling-or-subject, the exact case that motivated the experiment) pure semantic NEVER surfaces the framing-correction insight in top-10; hybrid puts it at #1 every run. On every other tested query, hybrid ties semantic (exact-fact queries semantic already nails at #1, leaving no room to improve, only room to break, which hybrid does not). Default tag weight 0.25 was slightly too hot and demoted one exact match #1->#2; tag=0.18 keeps the relational win and removes that regression. SHIPPED: chronicle_rag.py now defaults to hybrid at tag=0.18 with a --semantic-only escape hatch; original backed up at chronicle_rag.py.pre-hybrid.bak. CAVEAT held deliberately: n=6, queries+anchors self-authored, so this is hypothesis-strong not ground_truth. The Mythos miss-to-#1 is robust (you cannot fake semantic missing it); the ties are softer. Wants validation against queries an outside party (or Anthony) authors before being called settled.
